summary: The day after the threshold: The day ends, and {the one who marks it} asks {the one crossing} what comes next.
realLife: One life: A Vietnam-era Marine who worked thirty-five years for a city, he finished high school at seventy-two in night school, keeping a promise to his dying mother. His daughter cheered as he crossed the stage. He then enrolled in college. Another: A factory worker's daughter who gave birth in her senior year of high school, then went across the country to a top engineering school with her baby. She took the child to day care every morning and studied after bedtime. Her daughter names her as a role model. Another: She left school in the tenth grade in Vietnam to help her family, immigrated, worked for years, and enrolled in a high school equivalency class at forty-five. Her teacher kept encouraging her after a poor first test. She passed. Another: A sixteen-year-old in Texas who learned he would be a father, worked two jobs, and planned to drop out for an equivalency test. The principal offered a half-day schedule instead. He graduated with his baby at the ceremony, and the diploma later helped him join the army. Another: On a first retail job in the Christmas rush she froze at the register. A customer told her to take her time, which let her wait for a coworker to help. She says that patience shaped how she treats people for decades.
